natural: even a foot-rule is too short somewhere

meaning.en: Everyone and everything has weak points; nobody is perfect.
meaning.zh: 再长的尺子也有不够用的地方；比喻任何人或事物都有短处。

equivalents: no one is good at everything

examples.zh: 尺有所短，寸有所长，别小看新来的同事。
examples.en: A foot may be short somewhere and an inch long elsewhere, so don't underestimate the new colleague.

examples.zh: 再优秀的运动员也是尺有所短，总有不擅长的项目。
examples.en: Even the best athletes have weak points and events they are not good at.

examples.zh: 他明白尺有所短的道理，所以虚心向别人请教。
examples.en: He knows that everyone has shortcomings, so he asks others for advice humbly.

story.en: In 'The Divination', the diviner Zheng Zhanyin tells the exiled Qu Yuan that a foot is short in some places and an inch long in others.
story.zh: 《楚辞·卜居》：“夫尺有所短，寸有所长；物有所不足，智有所不明。”

usage.en: Usually paired with 寸有所长 ('an inch is long in places'). Used to encourage humility and mutual respect. Predicate or standalone saying.
usage.zh: 常与“寸有所长”连用，劝人谦虚、互相尊重；可作谓语或独立成句。

natural: the elders east of the river

meaning.en: The people of one's home region, especially those to whom one feels deeply indebted after failure.
meaning.zh: 指家乡的父老乡亲，常含有愧对乡亲之意。

examples.zh: 没混出名堂，他无颜见江东父老。
examples.en: Having made nothing of himself, he was ashamed to face the folk back home.

examples.zh: 衣锦还乡，终于对得起江东父老了。
examples.en: Returning home in glory, he had finally done right by the folk back home.

examples.zh: 在外打拼多年，他心中一直惦记着江东父老。
examples.en: After years away, he still carries his hometown elders in his heart.

story.en: After his defeat, Xiang Yu refuses to cross the river, saying that even if the elders of Jiangdong pitied him and made him king, how could he face them?
story.zh: 项羽兵败乌江，不肯渡江：“纵江东父老怜而王我，我何面目见之？”

usage.en: Literary, often in negative sentences like 无颜见江东父老. 'Jiangdong' is the Yangtze's lower reaches; today it means any home folk.
usage.zh: 书面语，常用于“无颜见江东父老”。江东本指长江下游，今泛指家乡父老。

natural: a pool of wine and a forest of meat

meaning.en: Extremely lavish and self-indulgent feasting, a mark of a decadent ruler.
meaning.zh: 形容极端奢侈、纵情享乐的生活。

examples.zh: 纣王沉迷酒池肉林，终致亡国。
examples.en: King Zhou was lost in debauchery and finally lost his kingdom.

examples.zh: 官员不能过着酒池肉林的生活。
examples.en: Officials must not live in decadent luxury.

examples.zh: 那场婚宴铺张得像酒池肉林。
examples.en: The wedding banquet was as extravagant as a decadent orgy.

story.en: The Records of the Grand Historian say King Zhou of Shang made a pool of wine and hung meat like a forest, so that men and women could feast naked.
story.zh: 《史记·殷本纪》：纣“以酒为池，县肉为林，使男女倮相逐其间，为长夜之饮”。

usage.en: Derogatory, about extravagance and hedonism. Predicate, object or attributive.
usage.zh: 贬义，指奢侈放纵、纵情享乐；可作谓语、宾语、定语。

natural: no telling the high from the low

meaning.en: Equal in quality, with nothing to choose between them.
meaning.zh: 分不出高低优劣，两者不相上下。

examples.zh: 两位选手实力相当，不分轩轾。
examples.en: The two contestants are well matched, with nothing to choose between them.

examples.zh: 这两本小说各有特色，不分轩轾。
examples.en: The two novels each have their strengths and are equal in merit.

examples.zh: 两队比分咬得很紧，不分轩轾。
examples.en: The two teams' scores were close, no difference between them.

usage.en: Literary; 轩 is the raised front of a carriage and 轾 the lowered one. Note 轾 is zhì and not 轻. Predicate.
usage.zh: 书面语。轩指车前高，轾指车前低。“轾”读 zhì，常被误写成“轻”。作谓语。

natural: a wise man's thousand thoughts

meaning.en: Even the wisest person, after a thousand deliberations, will make some mistake.
meaning.zh: 聪明的人考虑千百次，也难免有失误（后面常接“必有一失”）。

examples.zh: 智者千虑，必有一失，这次是我疏忽了。
examples.en: Even the wise slip up; this time I was careless.

examples.zh: 别太自责，智者千虑也有失手的时候。
examples.en: Don't blame yourself; even wise people slip up at times.

examples.zh: 智者千虑，必有一失，所以决策前要多听意见。
examples.en: Nobody is infallible, so listen to other opinions before deciding.

story.en: Li Zuoche tells Han Xin that a wise man's thousand thoughts must contain one mistake, and a fool's thousand thoughts one gain.
story.zh: 李左车对韩信说：“臣闻智者千虑，必有一失；愚者千虑，必有一得。”

usage.en: Normally quoted in full: 智者千虑，必有一失 (and the converse 愚者千虑，必有一得). Used to console someone or to excuse a slip politely.
usage.zh: 通常说全句“智者千虑，必有一失”，与“愚者千虑，必有一得”相对。多用于安慰人或委婉地为失误辩解。

natural: an ant trying to shake a tree

meaning.en: To attempt something far beyond one's strength; a ridiculous overestimate of oneself.
meaning.zh: 蚂蚁想摇动大树；比喻自不量力。

equivalents: an ant trying to topple a tree

examples.zh: 想靠一家小店挤垮连锁巨头，无异于蚍蜉撼树。
examples.en: A small shop trying to push out a chain giant is like an ant trying to shake a tree.

examples.zh: 他们的反对不过是蚍蜉撼树，改变不了大局。
examples.en: Their objections are an ant shaking a tree and can't change the outcome.

examples.zh: 个人对抗整个体制，难免蚍蜉撼树。
examples.en: A lone person against the whole system is bound to be an ant against a tree.

story.en: In 'Teasing Zhang Ji', Han Yu mocks those who run down Li Bai and Du Fu: an ant shaking a great tree, laughable that they don't know their limits.
story.zh: 韩愈《调张籍》：“蚍蜉撼大树，可笑不自量。”

usage.en: Derogatory, mocking those who underrate the odds. Often in the pattern 蚍蜉撼树，可笑不自量. 蚍蜉 is a big black ant.
usage.zh: 贬义，嘲笑自不量力的人；常说“蚍蜉撼树，可笑不自量”。蚍蜉指大黑蚁。

synonyms: 小娃娃扛大梁——自不量力

natural: a prominent head and horn

meaning.en: To stand out from the crowd, especially of a young person with outstanding ability.
meaning.zh: 比喻青少年才华、本领突出，超出常人。

equivalents: a young person who stands out

examples.zh: 这位年轻作家早已头角峥嵘。
examples.en: The young writer has long stood out.

examples.zh: 他自幼头角峥嵘，十六岁就考上了大学。
examples.en: He was exceptional from childhood and entered university at sixteen.

examples.zh: 几位头角峥嵘的新人让评委眼前一亮。
examples.en: A few rising stars made the judges sit up.

usage.en: Praise, mostly for the young. Predicate or attributive. Often interchangeable with 崭露头角, which stresses the moment of emerging.
usage.zh: 褒义，多指年轻人；作谓语、定语。与“崭露头角”近似，后者强调刚刚显露。

natural: fond of playing the teacher

meaning.en: To love lecturing others and set oneself up as an authority when one doesn't know that much.
meaning.zh: 喜欢以教导者自居，爱对别人指手画脚。

equivalents: a know-it-all who loves to preach

examples.zh: 他总爱好为人师，对谁都要指点两句。
examples.en: He always likes to play the teacher and gives everyone some tips.

examples.zh: 好为人师是学习进步的大敌。
examples.en: Loving to lecture others is the enemy of progress in learning.

examples.zh: 她从不好为人师，却乐于分享经验。
examples.en: She never plays the teacher but gladly shares what she has learned.

story.en: Mencius says that the fault of people is that they like to be teachers of others.
story.zh: 《孟子·离娄上》：“人之患在好为人师。”

usage.en: Derogatory, about arrogance. Do not use it for a real teacher who happens to enjoy teaching. 为 is read wéi.
usage.zh: 贬义，批评自以为是；不要用来夸真正乐于教人的老师。“为”读 wéi。

natural: cannot bear to read to the end

meaning.en: Too sad, or too poorly written, to bear reading through.
meaning.zh: 因内容悲惨或文章太差而不忍心读完。

equivalents: too painful to read to the end

examples.zh: 灾区的报道惨烈得让人不忍卒读。
examples.en: The reports from the disaster area were so harrowing that one couldn't bear to finish them.

examples.zh: 这篇论文漏洞百出，简直不忍卒读。
examples.en: The paper is so full of holes that it is painful to read.

examples.zh: 信里的字字句句都叫人不忍卒读。
examples.en: Every word in the letter was too heartbreaking to finish.

usage.en: Two senses: sorrowful content (most common) or poor writing. Literary; 卒 is read zú here ('finish').
usage.zh: 有两种用法：内容悲惨（最常见）或文章拙劣。书面语；“卒”读 zú，意为完毕。

natural: politely declining for lack of ability

meaning.en: A polite phrase for declining something, as if saying one is not capable of it.
meaning.zh: 谦辞，表示推辞，说自己能力不够，不能接受或照办。

examples.zh: 他请我去演讲，我只好敬谢不敏。
examples.en: He asked me to give a talk, and I had to politely decline.

examples.zh: 这种应酬，我向来敬谢不敏。
examples.en: I have always politely begged off such social gatherings.

examples.zh: 对于这样的提议，我只能敬谢不敏。
examples.en: I can only decline such a proposal with thanks.

usage.en: Formal, wry politeness; mostly used when you do not want to do something. It is not a general 'thank you' and it doesn't mean the speaker is truly incompetent.
usage.zh: 正式、略带幽默的客气话，多用于不愿做某事时的婉拒。不是一般的感谢，也不真表示无能。

natural: a bright mirror hung on high

meaning.en: Describes an upright, discerning judge or official who sees through every case.
meaning.zh: 比喻执法官员公正廉明，判案明察秋毫。

examples.zh: 法庭上方挂着“明镜高悬”的匾额。
examples.en: Above the courtroom hangs a plaque reading 'Bright Mirror on High'.

examples.zh: 百姓盼望的是一位明镜高悬的好法官。
examples.en: What ordinary people hope for is a judge of clear sight and fairness.

examples.zh: 这个案子能水落石出，全靠法官明镜高悬。
examples.en: The case was cleared up thanks to the judge's keen impartiality.

usage.en: Praise, mostly used for courts and officials, often on plaques. Variant 秦镜高悬 alludes to the Qin mirror said to reveal the heart.
usage.zh: 褒义，多用于法院、官员，常见于匾额。异形“秦镜高悬”用秦代传说中能照见人心的镜子。

natural: green leaves plump, red blossoms thin

meaning.en: Late spring, when leaves are lush and flowers are fading.
meaning.zh: 绿叶繁茂，红花凋零，指暮春时节的景象。

examples.zh: 雨后的庭院，已是绿肥红瘦的时节。
examples.en: After the rain the courtyard was in its lush-leaf, thin-bloom season.

examples.zh: 窗外绿肥红瘦，让她想起李清照的词。
examples.en: Outside, the leaves were thick and the flowers thin, reminding her of Li Qingzhao's poem.

examples.zh: 一场春雨后，满园绿肥红瘦。
examples.en: After a spring rain the garden was all thick leaves and few blossoms.

story.en: Li Qingzhao wakes after a night of wind and rain and asks the maid about the crab-apple blossoms; the answer is that they're unchanged, but she says surely the green is plump and the red thin.
story.zh: 李清照《如梦令》：“知否，知否？应是绿肥红瘦。”

usage.en: Literary and poetic; it describes scenery and carries a note of regret for spring passing. Not about people's weight.
usage.zh: 诗意的书面语，写景，带有惜春之意；与人的胖瘦无关。

natural: after three days apart

meaning.en: A person who has been apart three days may have changed so much that one must look at him anew, meaning people can improve quickly.
meaning.zh: 读书人分别几天就会有很大进步，应当用新眼光看待。

equivalents: look at someone with fresh eyes

examples.zh: 士别三日，刮目相看，他现在的英语流利极了。
examples.en: Three days apart and you must see him anew; his English is now excellent.

examples.zh: 士别三日，当另眼相看，别再拿老眼光看他了。
examples.en: Give him a fresh look after three days apart and stop judging him by old standards.

examples.zh: 士别三日，她的画技大有长进。
examples.en: In this short span her painting has made great strides.

origin.source: 《三国志·吴书·吕蒙传》裴松之注引《江表传》

story.en: Sun Quan urged Lü Meng to study; later Lu Su was amazed at his learning, and Lü Meng replied that a scholar apart for three days must be looked at with new eyes.
story.zh: 吕蒙答鲁肃：“士别三日，即更刮目相待。”

usage.en: Positive; encourage people to stay open to others' growth. Usually quoted with 刮目相看 as 士别三日，当刮目相看.
usage.zh: 褒义，提醒人们用发展的眼光看人；常与“刮目相看”连用。

natural: hunting for passages and picking phrases

meaning.en: To write or study by collecting fine phrases from books, without original thought.
meaning.zh: 只在书本里搜寻摘取现成词句，不能独立思考或创新。

examples.zh: 写文章若只是寻章摘句，就写不出真情实感。
examples.en: Writing that merely lifts phrases from other sources won't carry real feeling.

examples.zh: 他读书不求甚解，只会寻章摘句。
examples.en: He doesn't read for understanding and only picks out fine phrases.

examples.zh: 光靠寻章摘句，成不了学问。
examples.en: Merely hunting for phrases will never make you a scholar.

usage.en: Critical; 寻 is xún. Used of writing and study. Can also describe harmless careful reading of the classics in old texts, but today it is negative.
usage.zh: 贬义；“寻”读 xún。多指写作和治学。古书中偶有认真读书的意思，今天一般为贬义。

natural: an arrogant army will lose

meaning.en: A force that is overconfident and looks down on its enemy is bound to be defeated.
meaning.zh: 骄傲轻敌的军队一定会失败；泛指骄傲自满必遭失败。

examples.zh: 骄兵必败，球队赢了几场就飘了，结果输了关键一仗。
examples.en: Pride goes before a fall; the team got carried away by a few wins and lost the key game.

examples.zh: 牢记骄兵必败的道理，不可轻敌。
examples.en: Remember that arrogant forces lose, and never underestimate the enemy.

examples.zh: 骄兵必败，哀兵必胜。
examples.en: The arrogant army loses and the army with grief wins.

usage.en: A warning applied to teams, firms and individuals. Often paired with 哀兵必胜. Predicate or standalone proverb.
usage.zh: 警示语，用于球队、企业或个人；常与“哀兵必胜”对举，作谓语或独立成句。

synonyms: 天下古今之庸人，皆以一惰字致败；天下古今之才人，皆以一傲字致败

natural: holding a jade disc is itself the crime

meaning.en: Possessing a treasure or great talent invites envy and harm.
meaning.zh: 拥有珍宝或才能，会招来祸害。

examples.zh: 他有一身才华却遭排挤，真是怀璧其罪。
examples.en: His talent drew exclusion; it was a case of being punished for owning treasure.

examples.zh: 怀璧其罪，财不露白。
examples.en: Treasure brings trouble, so never show your wealth.

examples.zh: 她深知怀璧其罪，从不炫耀自己的专利。
examples.en: She knew treasure attracts trouble and never flaunted her patents.

story.en: When Yu Shu's brother wanted his jade, Yu Shu said a commoner is innocent but holding jade is his crime, and gave it up to avoid harm.
story.zh: 《左传·桓公十年》：“周谚有之：匹夫无罪，怀璧其罪。”

usage.en: Usually a sigh; 璧 is read bì. Do not read it as meaning the treasure holder is guilty.
usage.zh: 多用于感叹；“璧”读 bì。意思不是持宝者真有罪。

natural: lowering the brow and bending the waist

meaning.en: To bow and scrape before the powerful.
meaning.zh: 低头弯腰，形容没有骨气地巴结权贵。

examples.zh: 他宁可辞职，也不愿摧眉折腰事权贵。
examples.en: He would rather quit than bow and scrape to those in power.

examples.zh: 安能摧眉折腰事权贵，使我不得开心颜？
examples.en: How can I bow and scrape to the powerful and not be able to smile?

examples.zh: 她从不摧眉折腰，哪怕丢了饭碗。
examples.en: She never grovels, even if it costs her job.

story.en: Li Bai ends his poem on dreaming of Mount Tianmu: how could he bow and scrape to the great and powerful, and not be able to wear a happy face?
story.zh: 李白《梦游天姥吟留别》：“安能摧眉折腰事权贵，使我不得开心颜！”

usage.en: Derogatory and literary; the famous Li Bai line is quoted when refusing to flatter. 折腰 echoes Tao Yuanming, who would not bow for five pecks of rice.
usage.zh: 贬义，书面语；常引李白名句表示不肯奉承。“折腰”也让人联想到陶渊明不为五斗米折腰。

natural: as different as cloud and mud

meaning.en: A vast gap in position or quality, like that between the sky and the ground.
meaning.zh: 像天上的云和地下的泥一样，相差悬殊。

examples.zh: 豪门与平民的生活有云泥之别。
examples.en: The lives of the wealthy and ordinary people are worlds apart.

examples.zh: 同样的食材，大厨和新手做出的味道有云泥之别。
examples.en: With the same ingredients, a top chef and a beginner produce vastly different tastes.

examples.zh: 两家公司的实力有云泥之别。
examples.en: The two firms' strengths are poles apart.

usage.en: Describes status or quality; usually predicate, with 有 or 存在. Neutral, but implies one side is much lower.
usage.zh: 形容地位或质量差距，常作谓语，与“有”“存在”搭配；中性，含一方远低于另一方之意。

natural: a monkey wearing a cap

meaning.en: A person who looks dignified but is coarse inside, especially a power-holder with no real quality.
meaning.zh: 猕猴戴上帽子，装成人样；比喻外表像样，实质低劣，也指虚有其表的掌权者。

examples.zh: 他穿得西装革履，实则沐猴而冠。
examples.en: He dressed in a suit and tie, but it's all a monkey in a hat.

examples.zh: 这些沐猴而冠的新贵，终究不懂风雅。
examples.en: These upstarts in fine clothes never understood refinement.

examples.zh: 不要做沐猴而冠的人，要内外兼修。
examples.en: Don't be a showy fake; cultivate both inside and out.

story.en: When Xiang Yu refused to move his capital to Guanzhong, a man said that people called the Chu men monkeys in caps, and now it was true; Xiang Yu had him boiled alive.
story.zh: 有人讥讽项羽：“人言楚人沐猴而冠耳，果然。”项羽烹杀了他。

usage.en: Strongly derogatory; a literary insult. Note 沐猴 means a macaque, not a bathing monkey.
usage.zh: 强烈贬义，书面骂人话。“沐猴”指猕猴，不是洗澡的猴子。

natural: the plum dies in place of the peach

meaning.en: To sacrifice one thing or person in place of another; also, to take another's place or blame.
meaning.zh: 李树代替桃树死去；比喻以此代彼，或代人受过。

examples.zh: 他们用李代桃僵的办法，舍弃小市场保住了大客户。
examples.en: They gave up a small market to protect the big client.

examples.zh: 下属李代桃僵，替上司背了黑锅。
examples.en: The subordinate took the fall for his boss.

examples.zh: 这是兵法中的李代桃僵之计。
examples.en: This is the stratagem of the plum replacing the peach in the art of war.

story.en: The Han Yuefu poem 'The Cock Crows' says the peach grows by the well with a plum beside it; insects gnaw the peach roots and the plum dies in its place, so brothers should help each other.
story.zh: 乐府《鸡鸣》：“桃生露井上，李树生桃旁。虫来啮桃根，李树代桃僵。树木身相代，兄弟还相忘？”

usage.en: A stratagem name (no. 11 of the Thirty-Six) with two senses, tactical sacrifice or taking another's blame. Check the context.
usage.zh: 三十六计第十一计，有两种用法：战术上的牺牲，或代人受过，需看语境。

natural: the humiliation of crawling between someone's legs

meaning.en: Enduring a great disgrace for the sake of a larger goal.
meaning.zh: 受人侮辱而忍耐，比喻为了远大目标能忍受屈辱。

equivalents: bearing disgrace to achieve one's aims

examples.zh: 他创业时受过胯下之辱，却从没放弃。
examples.en: He swallowed humiliations while starting his business and never gave up.

examples.zh: 韩信忍受胯下之辱，终成一代名将。
examples.en: Han Xin endured the humiliation and became a great general.

examples.zh: 能忍胯下之辱的人才能成大事。
examples.en: Only one who can bear disgrace can accomplish great things.

story.en: A butcher's youth challenged Han Xin to stab him or crawl between his legs, and Han Xin lowered himself and crawled; the town laughed, but later he became a general.
story.zh: 《史记·淮阴侯列传》：市井少年侮辱韩信，让他从胯下爬过，韩信“孰视之，俯出胯下，蒲伏”。

usage.en: Mostly refers to Han Xin's story, used to praise patience. 胯 is kuà ('crotch').
usage.zh: 多指韩信的故事，用来赞扬隐忍；“胯”读 kuà。

natural: the old Ah Meng of the Wu region

meaning.en: A person of little learning; usually in the negation 'no longer the old Ah Meng', meaning someone who has greatly improved.
meaning.zh: 指学识浅陋的人；常用“非复吴下阿蒙”表示人已大有长进。

equivalents: 'not the man he used to be'

examples.zh: 几年不见，他早已不是吴下阿蒙了。
examples.en: After a few years apart he is no longer the unlearned boy he was.

examples.zh: 别以为我还是吴下阿蒙，这几年我下了不少功夫。
examples.en: Don't think I'm still the same ignoramus; I've worked a lot these years.

examples.zh: 他自嘲仍是吴下阿蒙，对新技术一窍不通。
examples.en: He jokes that he is still the same unlearned fellow, clueless about new tech.

origin.source: 《三国志·吴书·吕蒙传》裴松之注引《江表传》

story.en: Lu Su, impressed by Lü Meng's new learning, said he was no longer the old 'Ah Meng' of the Wu region.
story.zh: 鲁肃感叹：“卿今者才略，非复吴下阿蒙！”

usage.en: Usually negated (不是/非复吴下阿蒙) as praise. Used affirmatively it is mild self-mockery or a jab.
usage.zh: 多用否定形式表示夸赞；肯定形式则是自嘲或讽刺。

natural: Zhuangzi dreams of being a butterfly

meaning.en: Life is like a dream and the line between illusion and reality is blurred.
meaning.zh: 比喻人生如梦，虚实难辨。

examples.zh: 庄周梦蝶，到底是人梦见了蝶，还是蝶梦见了人？
examples.en: Zhuangzi dreamed of a butterfly; did the man dream the butterfly or the butterfly the man?

examples.zh: 这部电影的主题类似庄周梦蝶。
examples.en: The film's theme is like Zhuangzi's butterfly dream.

examples.zh: 他恍惚间有庄周梦蝶之感。
examples.en: He had a dazed Zhuangzi-and-butterfly feeling.

story.en: Zhuangzi once dreamt he was a butterfly; on waking he did not know whether he was Zhuang Zhou who had dreamt a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming it was Zhuang Zhou.
story.zh: 《庄子·齐物论》：“昔者庄周梦为胡蝶……不知周之梦为胡蝶与，胡蝶之梦为周与？”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Literary and philosophical; also written 蝶梦庄周. Used in discussions of illusion and reality, or the pointlessness of fixed distinctions.
usage.zh: 书面、哲理性强；也作“蝶梦庄周”，用于谈虚实、物我之辨。

synonyms: 昔者庄周梦为胡蝶，栩栩然胡蝶也

natural: the people matter more than the ruler

meaning.en: The people are the most important and the ruler the least.
meaning.zh: 百姓最重要，君主最轻。

equivalents: rulers are less important than the people

examples.zh: 孟子主张民贵君轻，对后世影响很大。
examples.en: Mencius argued that the people matter more than the ruler, a view that was very influential.

examples.zh: 民贵君轻的思想至今有现实意义。
examples.en: The idea of putting the people first is still relevant today.

examples.zh: 真正的好官懂得民贵君轻。
examples.en: A true good official understands that the people come first.

story.en: Mencius says the people are the most important, the altars of the land and grain come next, and the ruler is the lightest.
story.zh: 《孟子·尽心下》：“民为贵，社稷次之，君为轻。”

usage.en: A political slogan from Mencius; formal. Often cited when discussing people-centred governance.
usage.zh: 孟子的政治主张，较正式；常在谈以民为本时引用。

synonyms: 民为贵，社稷次之，君为轻
